query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA with an FCC matrix, elevated-temperature exposure in oxidizing gases leads to preferential oxidation and porous oxide scale formation along grain boundaries (primarily from reactive Ti and Cr), which in turn degrades the intergranular cohesion and promotes catastrophic failure. In contrast, reducing atmospheres suppress this oxidation‐induced damage.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with a single-phase FCC matrix and minimal preexisting oxide films.
generation.intervention: Alter the gaseous environment during elevated-temperature exposure by comparing oxidizing (oxygen-rich) conditions to reducing (low oxygen) conditions.
generation.conditions: Exposure at elevated temperatures (e.g., between 600°C and 800°C) for prolonged times under controlled gas atmospheres; tests conducted both in oxygen-rich and oxygen-deficient (reducing) environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundaries acting as sites for preferential oxide formation, leading to local embrittlement and crack initiation.
generation.mechanism: At high temperatures in oxidizing gases, Ti and Cr oxidize preferentially along grain boundaries, forming a porous, non-protective scale that induces internal stresses and weakens intergranular cohesion. This local degradation facilitates rapid crack propagation, explaining why catastrophic failure may occur under service conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Samples exposed to oxidizing conditions will exhibit pronounced grain-boundary oxidation, reduced intergranular fracture toughness, and an earlier onset of catastrophic failure compared to those exposed to reducing environments, which should show minimal grain-boundary oxidation and retain better mechanical integrity.
generation.baseline: The initial as-manufactured state with a homogeneous, FCC matrix and a minimal, continuous oxide layer.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable under high-temperature exposures (approximately 600–800°C) and for exposure times sufficient to allow measurable oxidation along grain boundaries; behavior outside this temperature/time domain or under extreme gas compositions may follow additional mechanisms.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the exact oxide phase compositions and the precise kinetics of oxidation at the grain boundaries. It is also unclear how minor alloying elements or processing-induced microstructural variations might modulate the oxidation behavior.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple samples of the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA and expose them to identical elevated-temperature conditions (600–800°C) in controlled atmospheres: one set in an oxidizing (oxygen-rich) environment and another set in a reducing (oxygen-deficient) environment. Conduct time-resolved microstructural analysis (using SEM/EDS and TEM) focusing on grain-boundary oxide formation and perform mechanical testing (e.g., intergranular fracture toughness and tensile tests) post-exposure.
measurements: Characterization of oxide scale thickness, morphology, and composition along grain boundaries.
Measurement of intergranular fracture toughness and overall tensile strength.
Comparison of crack initiation sites and propagation patterns between environments.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant difference in grain-boundary oxide formation and mechanical degradation (e.g., similar fracture toughness and tensile properties) is detected between samples exposed to oxidizing and reducing conditions, or if catastrophic failure does not preferentially correlate with the presence of grain-boundary oxidation, then the hypothesis is falsified.
